## [51] How to Get Your App to the Top of the Salesforce Apps List
Source: https://magicfuse.co/blog/top-of-the-salesforce-apps-list

On Salesforce AppExchange, visibility can make or break your app’s success. Web and mobile apps that rank higher in search results not only attract significantly more traffic but also experience a substantial increase in installs. In fact, studies suggest that top-ranked apps can get as much as 80% more visibility than those that appear further down the list, directly leading to higher engagement and conversions. For Salesforce ISVs, improving your app’s AppExchange ranking is crucial to standing out in an increasingly crowded marketplace.

But what steps can you take to rise to the top?

We’ll cover how to enhance your app’s listing with engaging content and marketing, establish credibility through user reviews, and build a community presence - all of which will boost your app’s visibility and drive installs. Ready to see your application in the top Salesforce apps list? Let’s dive into the steps to help you boost productivity and get your app to the top.

Keyword Optimization for AppExchange Listings

Keyword optimization is foundational to improving your app’s visibility on Salesforce AppExchange. By carefully selecting and strategically integrating relevant search terms, you can significantly boost your app’s chances of being discovered by potential users. It’s essential to understand how users search for apps on AppExchange and how to align your app’s listing with those search behaviors.

Conducting Keyword Research to Identify Relevant Search Terms

This research process involves understanding the language and keywords commonly used by your target audience - whether they are Salesforce administrators, business analysts, or IT professionals.

Use Salesforce-Specific Tools

Salesforce offers tools like the AppExchange search function and Salesforce Schema Builder. Salesforce Schema Builder is a tool that is strictly used to visualize and manage your data model within Salesforce. It lets you see and configure objects, fields, and relationships in a drag-and-drop interface, which is super helpful for understanding how your data is structured. Use these to analyze what terms appear frequently in competitor listings and compare the results of similar apps or competitors in your category.

Leverage Google Keyword Planner

Google Keyword Planner can be a helpful tool for identifying related keywords that are being searched on other digital platforms, even outside of Salesforce. Use it to discover high-traffic keywords that align with your app's functionality.

Many first-time ISV publishers assume Google-style SEO works 1:1 on AppExchange. That’s not true. Salesforce uses search keyword fields and metadata, and heavily weights ratings, installs, and engagement.

Check Competitor Listings

Browse through similar apps on AppExchange and pay close attention to their titles, descriptions, and keyword choices. Tools like Ahrefs or SEMrush can also provide detailed insight into the keywords competitors rank for their services, helping you target gaps in their keyword strategy.

Strategically Integrating Keywords in Titles, Descriptions, and "Search Keywords" Fields

Once you've identified your relevant keywords, the next step is integrating them into your AppExchange listing. Keyword optimization isn't just about stuffing terms into your title or description; it’s about incorporating them in a way that reads naturally and enhances your app’s appeal.

Titles

Your app’s title is one of the most important places to use your keywords. The title should communicate what your app does and include the most relevant search term. A concise, keyword-rich title suits SEO and helps potential users immediately understand what your app offers.

Descriptions

Your app description should provide a detailed overview of the features and benefits while naturally incorporating your target keywords. Consider how users will phrase their needs when searching for an app that solves their problems. Use relevant keywords in the first 100-150 characters, as this is what potential users see first.

"Search Keywords" Fields

Salesforce AppExchange allows you to include "Search Keywords" in the AppExchange Publisher Console, which help categorize and rank your app within the platform. Keep in mind that you have a 256-character limit for these keywords. It's essential to use a combination of specific and broad terms that reflect your app’s core functionalities to drive optimal search traffic.

Avoid Keyword Stuffing

While it’s essential to use keywords strategically, avoid overstuffing your listing with excessive keywords. Like Google’s, Salesforce’s algorithms can penalize listings that appear unnatural or spammy. Focus on a few well-researched, high-impact keywords and integrate them into your content.

Practical Tips for Keyword Optimization
Use Long-Tail Keywords: Besides broad keywords, incorporate long-tail keywords (e.g., "Salesforce sales automation for small businesses") to target more specific user needs. These tend to have lower competition and can attract more qualified leads.
Monitor Trends: As Salesforce evolves, keywords can change over time. To stay on top of trending search terms within the Salesforce ecosystem, subscribe to forums and Salesforce blogs or use tools like Google Trends.
Refine Regularly: Keyword optimization isn’t a one-time task. Monitor your app’s performance on AppExchange and adjust your keywords based on new trends, user feedback, or market shifts.
Engaging Visual Content

Visual content is crucial for making your Salesforce AppExchange listing stand out. High-quality screenshots and demo videos help users clearly understand your app’s functionality and features, leading to better engagement and higher installs.

High-Quality Screenshots

Screenshots give potential users a first look at your app. Ensure your images are clear, focused, and showcase your app's key features. Highlight unique functionalities with annotations, such as "Customizable Dashboards" or "Real-time Analytics." Avoid clutter and make each screenshot visually appealing to help users quickly grasp the app’s value.

Ensure screenshots follow AppExchange image guidelines: JPEG/PNG format, 1280x720 resolution, and max 10 screenshots per listing.

Adding brief annotations or arrows to your screenshots can guide users' attention to important features. For instance, if your app integrates customer preferences and Salesforce data from multiple sources, highlight this functionality with a note like “Seamlessly integrates customer data from X, Y, Z systems.”

Demo Videos

A concise, 1-2 minute demo video can effectively showcase how your app works in action. Focus on key features, show real use cases, and keep the video clear and engaging. Narration and text overlays can enhance understanding, and optimizing the video for mobile ensures it’s accessible on all devices.

If your app automates email marketing within Salesforce platform, create a demo video that walks the viewer through the setup process, the templates available, and how to send personalized emails. As you describe and demonstrate these features, include text captions like "Set up in minutes" or "Automatically segment your contacts" to make it clear how users benefit.

Building Community Connections

Building strong community connections within the Salesforce ecosystem is a powerful way to boost your app’s visibility and credibility. Active participation in Salesforce user groups, forums, and events helps establish your app as a trusted solution, while engaging directly with potential users and sales teams builds meaningful relationships.

Active Participation in Salesforce User Groups, Forums, and Community Events

Salesforce’s vibrant community provides numerous opportunities for developers to interact with potential customers. By actively engaging in Salesforce user groups and forums, you not only stay up-to-date on industry trends but also build a network of loyal users and business together.

Participate in local and online user groups focused on Salesforce topics related to your app. This is a great way to connect with people who are already using Salesforce and might be interested in your app.

Contribute to discussions on forums like the Salesforce Developer Community or the Salesforce Stack Exchange. Answering questions and providing helpful insights and solutions can build your reputation as an expert in your field.

Leveraging Webinars and Q&A Sessions

Webinars and Q&A sessions provide your company with a platform to interact with potential users in real-time, showcasing your app’s features and addressing user concerns directly. Hosting educational webinars can help you demonstrate your app’s value and answer common questions, while building trust through transparent communication.

Organize webinars to demonstrate your app’s features in action. This allows you to show potential users how your app can solve their specific problems. Be sure to provide a clear agenda and keep the session interactive.

Host live Q&A sessions where users can ask questions about your app, implementation, and best practices. These sessions foster trust and help clarify any doubts.

Encouraging User Reviews and Ratings

User reviews and ratings are crucial for building credibility and improving your app's ranking on AppExchange. Positive reviews increase trust, while constructive feedback helps you improve your app.

Deliver Exceptional Value: Ensure your app meets user needs and offers clear benefits. Satisfied users are more likely to leave positive reviews.
Request Reviews: Politely ask satisfied users to leave a review. Include a simple call to action after successful interactions or support resolutions.
Offer Incentives: Consider offering incentives, such as extended trials or exclusive features, in exchange for feedback.
Respond Promptly: Acknowledge both positive and negative feedback quickly. Show appreciation for positive reviews and address concerns professionally.
Act on Feedback: Regularly update your app based on user suggestions, demonstrating your commitment to continuous improvement.
Content Marketing for Visibility

Content marketing is a powerful strategy for driving visibility and establishing thought leadership in your category within the Salesforce ecosystem. By creating valuable, engaging content around your app’s value, you can not only attract potential users but also increase your app’s credibility and organic reach.

Write informative blog posts, case studies, and articles that focus on your app’s core value proposition. Address common challenges that your target audience faces, and show how your app can solve these issues.

For example, if your app helps automate data entry within Salesforce, write a post about how automation can improve efficiency and reduce errors in CRM data management.

Video content, especially product demos or explainer videos, is an excellent way to show your app in action. Videos help users visualize how your app solves their problems, making it more compelling than static images or text alone. Demonstrate the app’s key features and explain how it integrates with Salesforce to streamline processes.

Sharing your blog posts, articles, and videos on social media platforms such as LinkedIn, Twitter, and Facebook helps increase organic reach. Social media enables you to connect directly with your audience and share valuable insights. Engage with your followers through comments, shares, and discussions, turning your content into a conversation that builds trust and interest in your app.

Adding Value Through Free Trials and Demos

Offering a free trial or live demo is one of the most effective ways to reduce onboarding friction and accelerate adoption. It gives prospective users hands-on experience with your app, allowing them the ability to assess its value before committing. This transparency can make your app stand out in the Salesforce AppExchange ecosystem - where competition is high and trust matters.

A free trial allows users to explore your app’s features at their own pace. Whether it's a 7-day or 30-day trial, this approach builds user confidence and shortens the sales cycle.

Make onboarding easy: Include in-app guidance, tooltips, or a quick-start checklist. Tools like WalkMe or Whatfix can enhance the trial experience.
Limit risk, not features: Instead of limiting functionality, consider limiting usage time. This lets users truly understand your app’s capabilities.

Live demo sessions are a great tool that offers a structured opportunity to showcase your app’s strengths and answer questions in real time. They work especially well for complex apps that benefit from guided explanations.

Host regular group demos: Offer weekly 20–30-minute walkthroughs with time for Q&A. Platforms like Zoom or Demio work well for this format.
Tailor demos to roles: Create different demos for Salesforce admins, sales teams, or IT managers, depending on their needs.
Offer recorded sessions: Provide an on-demand demo video on your AppExchange listing or website so users can view it at their convenience.
Using Analytics to Optimize Your App

Analytics are a game changer for understanding how users engage with your app listing, and where there’s room to improve. By tracking metrics like page views, trial activations, and user behavior, you can refine your AppExchange strategy for better visibility and conversion rates.

Start by regularly tracking the performance of your listing and user engagement metrics:

Salesforce doesn’t currently offer deep in-platform analytics for AppExchange listings, but you can use tools like UTM parameters and Google Analytics to track traffic from external content, campaigns, and referral links.

Conclusion

Getting to the top of the Salesforce AppExchange listings isn’t a one-time effort; it’s an ongoing process that requires strategic focus, community engagement, and continuous optimization. From keyword-rich listings and compelling visuals to user-driven reviews and community involvement, every element plays a role in how your app is discovered and trusted.

To maintain a strong presence, regularly update your listing with fresh content, respond to user feedback, and stay involved in Salesforce communities. Apps that evolve with user needs and platform trends not only rise in rankings but also build lasting customer loyalty.

Need help getting there? At MagicFuse, we specialize in helping Salesforce ISVs build, launch, and grow high-performing best Salesforce apps. Whether you need support with development, security review, or optimizing your listing - we’ve got you covered. Contact us to take your AppExchange strategy to the next level.

FAQs
How can I optimize my AppExchange listing for better visibility?

Use relevant keywords in your title, description, and search fields. Include high-quality visuals, and a compelling value proposition, and encourage positive reviews. Regularly update the content based on performance metrics and user feedback.

What are effective ways to increase user reviews on AppExchange?

Ask for reviews after customer success with interactions, offer incentives like extended trials, and make it easy for users to leave feedback. Always respond to positive and negative reviews to show you value user input.

How to Choose the Best Salesforce Consulting Partner

Selecting the right partner from the top Salesforce consultants in 2026 requires more than checking certifications or hourly rates; it’s about finding a team that can help your organization thrive in the AI-native, data-connected, and multi-cloud world Salesforce suite now enables. As platform complexity grows with Agentforce, Revenue Cloud, and Data Cloud, the partner you choose should demonstrate not only configuration skills but also a strategic understanding of consulting services, data architecture, automation, and business transformation to maximize your Salesforce investment.

1. Define Your Business Needs and Outcomes

Start by clarifying what you want Salesforce to achieve for your organization, not just what modules to deploy. Are you optimizing your sales operations, enabling self-service portals, or implementing predictive analytics through Agentforce? Document measurable outcomes (e.g., “reduce case resolution time by 30%” or “unify customer data sources into a single Data Cloud view”). A strong consulting partner will challenge and refine these goals, aligning them with achievable technical roadmaps.

2. Evaluate Multi-Cloud and AI Readiness

In 2026, Salesforce transformation often spans multiple clouds: Sales, Service, Marketing, AI integration, Revenue, and Data Cloud, connected through APIs and MuleSoft. When vetting partners, look for:

Proven experience deploying or integrating Revenue Cloud, including advanced quote-to-cash and subscription billing.
Demonstrated expertise in Data Cloud setup, data modeling, ingestion pipelines, and identity resolution.
Real-world Agentforce or Einstein AI implementations for lead scoring, service automation, or forecasting.
Ask for case studies that show how the firm used AI and automation to improve tangible business KPIs.
3. Review Digital Transformation Portfolios, Not Just Implementations

A partner’s ability to deliver business transformation is far more valuable than simply performing Salesforce setup or migration. Review whether they’ve executed end-to-end programs that included:

Process reengineering or operating model design.
Integration with ERP, finance, or data warehouses.
Post-launch optimization (e.g., continuous AI tuning, analytics adoption, user enablement).
Check if their work has been recognized through Salesforce Partner Innovation Awards, AppExchange case studies, or third-party client references.
4. Assess Technical Depth and Certifications

While certifications alone don’t guarantee excellence, they reveal the firm’s technical maturity and breadth. In particular, ensure your potential partner has expertise across:

Architect and Developer tracks (for custom solutions and scalability).
Data Cloud Consultant, AI Associate, or Agentforce Developer credentials.
Revenue Cloud, CPQ, and Billing certifications for finance and sales alignment.
Also, verify their experience with governance tools such as Copado, Gearset, or DevOps Center for release management and compliance.
5. Consider Industry Experience and Security Practices

Partners with proven knowledge of your industry can accelerate discovery and reduce implementation risk. Whether in healthcare, financial services, SaaS, or manufacturing, domain familiarity helps consultants configure Salesforce around the nuances of regulations, workflows, and KPIs.

Additionally, ensure that your partner follows Salesforce’s Well-Architected Framework, data residency standards, and security review best practices for integrations and managed packages.

6. Validate Delivery Model and Post-Implementation Support

Hybrid and remote delivery have become standard across the ecosystem. The best partners combine on-site collaboration during discovery with remote agile sprints for execution, ensuring scalability and cost efficiency.

Post-implementation, ask about their approach to:

Ongoing AI model retraining and Data Cloud maintenance.
Performance monitoring and technical debt reduction.
User enablement, training, and governance cadence.
7. Check References and Customer Satisfaction Metrics

Request recent client testimonials, especially from 2024–2025 projects. Reputable partners should be transparent about their Net Promoter Score (NPS), retention rate, and AppExchange rating, as well as providing access to certified Salesforce experts. Direct client feedback provides the clearest insight into how the partner manages communication, risk, and long-term value delivery.

Red Flags When Hiring a Salesforce Consultant

Knowing what to look for in top Salesforce consulting firms is half the job. The other half? Spotting warning signs early — before they become expensive lessons.

No plan for Data Cloud or AI. If a partner still treats Salesforce as a standalone CRM and can't explain how Data Cloud or Agentforce fits your roadmap, they're working from a pre-2024 playbook. You deserve a partner who's already building with these tools, not one planning to learn on your project.

All configuration, no code. Declarative tools work for straightforward orgs. But when you're connecting multiple clouds, building custom integrations, or scaling for thousands of users, you need Apex, LWC, and API expertise. Ask to see their developer-level certifications — not just Admin credentials.

Vague case studies with no numbers. "We helped a client improve operations" tells you nothing. Look for specific outcomes: "reduced case resolution time by 40%" or "unified 3 data sources into a single Data Cloud view." If a firm can't show recent, detailed results from 2024–2025 projects, keep looking.

No post-launch support model. A Salesforce rollout doesn't end at go-live. New features ship 3 times a year, technical debt accumulates, and users need ongoing enablement. If your partner's engagement ends at deployment, you'll be on your own when things break — or when Agentforce capabilities you should be using go untouched.

No DevOps or governance strategy. Without proper release management (Copado, Gearset, or similar), version control, and sandbox discipline, even well-architected orgs deteriorate quickly. Ask how they handle deployments, rollbacks, and compliance — vague answers here signal trouble later.

Cookie-cutter proposals. If the SOW arrives before discovery — before the partner understands your processes, tech stack, and industry requirements — that's a template, not a strategy. The best Salesforce CRM consulting providers tailor every engagement to your specific goals and constraints.

Shallow certification profiles. Administrator certification is a starting point, not a differentiator. For complex projects, you need Architect, Platform Developer II, Data Cloud Consultant, and Revenue Cloud credentials on the team. A firm with 50 consultants and only Admin certs has a low technical ceiling — and your project will hit it.

How Did We Evaluate These Companies?

Our 2026 evaluation framework reflects how the Salesforce ecosystem has evolved, from traditional CRM deployments to AI-driven, multi-cloud, data-connected solutions. Each consulting firm from the top Salesforce consulting companies was assessed across the following key dimensions:

1. Technical & Cloud Expertise

We analyzed each company’s experience across major Salesforce clouds, Sales, Service, Marketing, Experience, Revenue, and Data Cloud, along with their ability to deliver full lifecycle projects from architecture to managed services.

2. AI and Agentforce Readiness

Partners were evaluated on their real-world use of Agentforce and Einstein AI for automation, forecasting, and customer insights, as well as their adherence to Salesforce’s trust and security standards.

3. Data Cloud & Multi-Cloud Integration

We prioritized consultancies capable of unifying customer data and orchestrating business processes across multiple Salesforce clouds and third-party systems via MuleSoft or API-led integration.

4. Innovation & Ecosystem Contribution

Companies developing AppExchange products, contributing to Salesforce’s PDO program, or winning Partner Innovation Awards received higher marks for advancing the ecosystem.

5. Client Results & Certifications

We reviewed verified client feedback, AppExchange ratings, and the breadth of certifications held, particularly in Architect, Revenue Cloud, and AI/Data Cloud roles, as indicators of technical maturity.

6. Delivery Model & Global Collaboration

Finally, we assessed partners’ ability to execute projects through hybrid and remote models, leveraging agile processes, real-time collaboration, and post-implementation support frameworks, with a focus on process development .

Conclusion

The Salesforce landscape in 2026 is defined by intelligent automation, data unification, and agentic AI, transforming how organizations engage customers and operate across clouds. Choosing the right top Salesforce consultant now means selecting a team that can do more than implement Salesforce - it’s about finding one that can architect, automate, provide custom development, and evolve your digital ecosystem as your business grows.

The companies featured in this list represent the forefront of that transformation, each driving innovation through Agentforce, Data Cloud, and multi-cloud integration. Yet among them, MagicFuse stands out for its deep technical expertise, ISV-grade engineering standards, and early adoption of Salesforce’s newest AI and automation capabilities.

If your organization is ready to modernize its Salesforce ecosystem, accelerate AI-driven efficiency, or bring a complex multi-cloud vision to life, MagicFuse is here to help.

Core Salesforce Services Offered by Certified Salesforce Partners

End-to-end Salesforce implementation across Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Marketing Cloud, and Financial Services Cloud with clear SOWs and measurable key services. Proper implementation ensures clean data models, accurate reporting, and a system users can adopt quickly.

2. Salesforce Application Development

Developers build tailored applications using Apex, Visualforce, and Lightning. This can mean advanced CPQ engines, partner portals, or custom integrations that connect Salesforce to ERP, billing, or marketing platforms.

Specialists use the Lightning Web Components framework to create fast, modern interfaces and mobile apps. This improves usability, speeds up workflows, and drives higher adoption across sales and support teams.

4. AppExchange Development

For companies needing repeatable solutions, a Salesforce consulting firm designs managed and unmanaged packages for the AppExchange. These can serve internal teams or become commercial apps offered to the broader Salesforce ecosystem.

5. Migration Services

They move data and processes from legacy CRMs or spreadsheets into Salesforce without corruption or downtime. This includes field mapping, deduplication, and connecting historical data to new automation rules.

6. AI & Automation Integration

Partners implement Einstein AI for predictive analytics, lead scoring, and sales forecasting while automating routine workflows to cut manual work and shorten sales cycles.

7. Salesforce Health Check

A comprehensive audit of your Salesforce org that assesses system performance, security, and configuration against Salesforce best practices. Certified consultants identify technical debt, misconfigurations, and optimization opportunities, then provide a roadmap for improving data quality, system efficiency, and user adoption. Regular Health Checks ensure your Salesforce environment scales effectively with your business.

8. Offshore & Outsourced Development

Hiring non-U.S. Salesforce platform developers to work onshore has become increasingly costly, with U.S. work visa sponsorships now reaching up to $100,000 per employee when factoring in legal fees, compliance, and administrative overhead. Instead of relocating talent, many businesses turn to offshore and outsourced Salesforce development.

Client testimonials and reviews can be found on independent platforms like AppExchange or Clutch, providing insights into reliability and quality of service.

5. Security Expertise

Your Salesforce CRM holds sensitive data. Verify the partner’s understanding of Salesforce Shield, data encryption, field-level security, SSO, and access controls to protect against breaches and maintain compliance.

6. Pricing Transparency

Transparency in pricing is important when selecting a Salesforce development partner to avoid surprise costs. Avoid unpleasant surprises by asking for a clear pricing model, including potential add-ons like data migration, API integrations, or post-launch support to reduce costs. Industry-Specific Use Cases
Finance & Banking

Financial institutions must balance customer experience with heavy regulatory oversight to gain valuable insights . Development partners often design end-to-end systems that automate complex approval chains and keep data secure.

For example, a bank issuing personal loans might replace its paper-heavy process with a Salesforce-based digital loan origination system. The platform could guide applicants through eligibility checks, automate credit scoring via third-party APIs, and trigger underwriting approvals without manual intervention. Compliance is built in through Salesforce Shield encryption, audit trails, and strict field-level security to satisfy KYC and AML regulations.

Wealth management firms benefit from 360-degree client dashboards that combine CRM data with investment platforms. Advisors can see portfolio performance, communications history, and risk profiles in one place, while Einstein AI flags high-value leads or accounts at risk of churn. These use cases illustrate how Salesforce becomes not just a sales tool, but a regulated, insight-driven hub for client relationships.

Healthcare & Life Sciences

Healthcare providers and life sciences companies face strict privacy laws and fragmented patient data. Salesforce development experts adapt the platform to support care delivery while keeping HIPAA compliance intact.

A hospital group, for instance, might use Salesforce to centralize patient interactions by integrating with existing EHR/EMR systems. Scheduling can be automated so that when a physician orders a follow-up test, the patient instantly receives appointment options, reminders, and secure messaging through an Experience Cloud portal. Access is restricted to authorized roles, and every action is logged for compliance.

Life sciences companies can use Salesforce to manage clinical trial recruitment by tracking participants, approvals, and communications in a secure and compliant way. AI features such as Einstein Bots and Agentforce can triage patient inquiries or provide context-aware support for staff, reducing administrative bottlenecks and improving patient satisfaction.

Retail & E-Commerce

Retail success increasingly depends on connecting digital and physical experiences. Salesforce enables this by unifying customer data, marketing, and order management into a single platform.

Imagine an apparel retailer running both brick-and-mortar stores and an online shop. A Salesforce partner could build an omnichannel platform that syncs inventory across warehouses and stores, powers real-time order status updates, and automates returns. Marketing Cloud might analyze shopping behavior to launch personalized campaigns, while Data Cloud consolidates in-store purchases with online browsing history to fuel predictive recommendations.

Another scenario: a specialty retailer launches a loyalty program fully embedded in Salesforce, where customer profiles update instantly when purchases are made across channels. Personalized rewards and mobile wallet integrations keep customers engaged, while automation streamlines fulfillment and return logistics.

Manufacturing & Industrial

Manufacturers often struggle to connect complex sales cycles, global supply chains, and field service operations. Salesforce development companies customize the platform to bring these moving parts into a single digital thread.

For example, an industrial equipment maker might deploy Salesforce to quote highly configurable products using CPQ and Revenue Cloud. Once an order is placed, data flows to ERP and supply chain systems, while customers and distributors track progress through a partner portal.

IoT integration adds another layer of efficiency. Machines in the field can feed performance data back to Salesforce; if a sensor detects a fault, it automatically creates a service case and schedules a technician through Field Service Lightning. Service teams arrive prepared with full asset history, improving uptime and reducing warranty costs.

These transformations turn Salesforce into more than a CRM; it becomes the digital backbone of manufacturing operations, connecting sales, service, and production in real time.

Implementation Best Practices
Define a Precise Scope of Work (SOW)

Start with absolute clarity on what will be delivered. A solid SOW breaks the project into concrete features, integrations, and business outcomes, along with dependencies and assumptions. For example, if the goal is to implement Sales Cloud with CPQ, the SOW should define lead-to-quote workflows, approval logic, data sources, and any third-party systems involved. Clear scope prevents mid-project drift and helps control both cost and timeline.

Align on Timelines and Milestones

Large Salesforce programs often fail when deadlines are vague or overly aggressive. Work with your development partner to set realistic milestones: discovery, design, development, UAT (user acceptance testing), training, and go-live. Each phase should have tangible deliverables such as prototypes, configured objects, or migration test runs. Transparent milestone tracking keeps executives informed and avoids last-minute surprises.

Prepare and Structure Your Data Early

Data is the foundation of Salesforce success. Clean, deduplicate, and normalize records before migration to avoid polluting the new system with inconsistencies. At the same time, plan API and integration strategies upfront; define how Salesforce will exchange data with ERP, marketing automation, payment, or support systems. This early work prevents broken processes and costly retrofits after go-live.

Train Teams and Manage Change Proactively

Even the best technical build fails without adoption. Provide role-based training tailored to sales, service, and leadership users, and communicate changes early so teams understand why the system matters. Consider “change champions” within each department to promote usage and provide feedback. Strong change management turns Salesforce from “another tool” into an essential part of daily work.

Monitor, Measure, and Continuously Optimize

The launch is not the finish line; it’s the beginning of performance tuning. Set up dashboards and KPIs to measure adoption, pipeline health, case resolution speed, and revenue impact. Utilize AI-driven insights (Einstein, Agentforce) to predict bottlenecks and identify opportunities for automation. A structured post-launch support plan keeps the system aligned with business growth.

ROI and Metrics

A Salesforce program pays for itself when delivery speed, automation, adoption, and operating costs move in the right direction, and you can prove it. Below is a pragmatic way to frame value, with concrete outcomes drawn from recent projects and published Salesforce customer stories.

Reduced Deployment Time

Shorter build cycles mean earlier value capture and fewer months of parallel systems. Teams that standardize scope, reuse accelerators, and automate QA typically compress timelines by 20–40%.

For example, for Atamis (ISV, procurement), a Salesforce-certified team stabilized a complex codebase, delivered urgent fixes faster than the client’s estimate, and established a clean release workflow, bringing features to users sooner while keeping Classic-and-Lightning compatibility intact. For Elements.cloud, they engineered and shipped a security-review–ready managed package to AppExchange, removing a common source of delays at launch.

Salesforce in the field: OpenTable launched its first Agentforce support agent in under a month and reached 73% case resolution within three weeks, handling ~11k conversations weekly, evidence that AI agents can compress service go-live and start producing results immediately.

How to measure: planned vs. actual go-live date; % of stories hitting sprint acceptance; time from UAT start to launch; time-to-first-value (e.g., first automated case, first automated quote).

Increased Automation and Efficiency

Automation reduces swivel-chair work, improves data quality at the source, and frees specialists to focus on higher-value tasks.

Elements.cloud (“Painkiller” app): reliable sync pipelines handling up to 50M records, AWS Lambda–driven data population, granular logging, and optimized queries, turning what used to be manual clean-up into repeatable, automated hygiene at scale.
ID-Pal(ISV, identity): bi-directional authorization and data exchange inside Salesforce via a managed package; reviewers can validate documents in-org and push changes back securely, no manual re-entry.
Purlos (EdTech): dynamic data mapping with Custom Metadata and multi-ingest (REST, SFTP, HubSpot, AWS, Experience Cloud) plus AI-assisted template creation, cutting manual prep and speeding student communications.
Prudential: Agentforce is projected to save wholesalers hours per week by capturing post-meeting notes, logging insights, and generating follow-ups, time redirected to advisor relationships and pipeline.
Good360: resource-matching agents are expected to save ~1,000 hours annually and make donation distribution 3× faster, while reducing carbon footprint by ~20%.

How to measure: automation coverage (% of processes with flows/bots), tasks or minutes saved per user per week, first-contact resolution, SLA adherence, cases/opportunities handled per FTE.

Improved CRM Adoption and User Satisfaction

Adoption determines whether dashboards reflect reality and whether automation fires when it should. Clear UX, fewer clicks, and trustworthy data lift usage and satisfaction.

De Gruyter Brill Poland: org health check, deduped data, security/access redesign, and full Service Cloud rollout (with routing and lifecycle automation) improved mobile usability and day-to-day efficiency, conditions that drive sustained adoption.
Nomagic & Ascent Solutions: Experience Cloud portals and custom LWCs (including reservation and sales calendars) gave partners and sellers interfaces purpose-built for their work, reducing friction and repeat questions.
Equinox: Agentforce turns a multi-screen booking flow into a natural conversation, guiding members to classes and handling routine requests, freeing concierge staff for white-glove service and raising digital CSAT.
OpenTable: AI agents resolve the bulk of simple inquiries, improving response times and letting human reps focus on complex cases, an adoption flywheel where faster answers bring more users to the channel.

How to measure: DAU/MAU for target profiles, time-in-task (clicks to complete), CSAT/NPS per channel, Knowledge deflection rate, training completion and follow-up quiz scores.

Cost Savings from Optimized Workflows

When processes are standardized and data is unified, support, sales ops, and engineering spend less on rework and ad-hoc fixes.

Elements.cloud: automated discovery of org technical debt and field usage visibility curbs unnecessary customizations and clean-up projects, hard savings that recur every quarter.
Atamis: higher test coverage, disciplined release cadence, and DocuSign integration reduce regression costs and third-party swivel work.
OpenTable: a 40% lift in automated resolution versus their prior bot (within the first three weeks) lowers cost per contact and preserves human capacity for onboarding and nuanced support.
Good360: smarter routing cuts miles traveled and wasted inventory, translating directly into logistics savings and measurable environmental impact.

How to measure: cost per case/lead/opportunity, engineer hours per release, rework/defect rates, integration/OPEX spend before vs. after, shipping and handling cost per unit (for ops-heavy orgs).

Turning Results Into a Business Case

Anchor your ROI model to a simple, defensible calculation:

Time savings: (minutes saved per user per week × # users × 48 weeks) ÷ 60 × blended hourly rate.
Automation lift: incremental cases/orders handled without headcount × cost per item.
Revenue impact: (conversion rate ↑ × avg. deal size) or (retention ↑ × gross margin).
Cost avoidance: reduced tool overlap, lower maintenance, fewer custom fixes, audit remediations avoided.
Add a payback view: Payback period = Total program cost ÷ monthly net benefit. For AI/Agentforce pilots, track a separate line for “digital labor capacity”, interactions handled autonomously × historical handle-time × hourly rate.

How do I choose the best Salesforce implementation partner and Salesforce consulting services for my business?

How much does Salesforce implementation typically cost?

The cost of implementing Salesforce varies depending on the complexity of your requirements, the size of your organization, and the level of customization needed. Smaller projects may cost $10,000 to $50,000, while larger, more complex implementations can exceed $100,000.

FAQ
Is Marketing Cloud the same as Account Engagement (Pardot)?

No. Salesforce Marketing Cloud (formerly ExactTarget) is a marketing automation platform focused on B2C engagement, driving personalized campaigns across multiple channels such as email, mobile, web, and social. Account Engagement (Pardot), on the other hand, is built for B2B demand generation and longer sales cycles, aligning tightly with Sales Cloud and Salesforce CRM to nurture leads and measure pipeline impact.

What does a Marketing Cloud consultant actually deliver in month 1–3?

During the first three months of a Salesforce Marketing Cloud implementation, certified consultants typically:

1  - Conduct business discovery and data management audits.

2 - Configure Marketing Cloud Connect to integrate with Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, or Commerce Cloud.

3 - Set up key Marketing Cloud products such as Email Studio, Journey Builder, and Automation Studio for initial marketing campaigns.

4 - Define audience segmentation and personalization logic using Data Cloud and Interaction Studio.

5 - Launch pilot cross-channel campaigns, optimize campaign flows, and enable your marketing team through workshops and knowledge transfer.

Which Salesforce Marketing Cloud solutions should we start with?

Most organizations begin with Marketing Cloud Engagement for email, mobile, and multi-channel campaigns. Then they expand to Salesforce Data Cloud for customer data unification and Audience Studio for segmentation. As they mature, teams add Marketing Cloud Personalization (formerly Interaction Studio) to deliver dynamic content and personalized journeys, followed by Advertising Studio and Mobile Studio to scale engagement across all touchpoints.

How does Salesforce Data Cloud improve Marketing Cloud results?

Salesforce Data Cloud connects and harmonizes data from Salesforce CRM, ecommerce, and third-party platforms into a single, unified view. This allows Salesforce Marketing Cloud experts to create precise audiences, trigger real-time personalization, and measure campaign analytics more accurately. It reduces data activation latency, fuels data-driven decision making, and helps marketing teams continually optimize campaigns for better customer engagement and ROI.

What certifications should our consultant have?

Look for credentials such as Marketing Cloud Engagement Consultant, Marketing Cloud Email Specialist, Data Cloud Consultant, and Administrator or Platform Developer I for integration and customization work. These validate hands-on expertise across key SFMC functions.

What integrations are ‘must-haves’?

Core integrations include Marketing Cloud Connect (linking SFMC to Sales and Service Clouds), Data Cloud ingestion connectors, and analytics integrations like Tableau or Google Analytics 360. Optional but valuable add-ons include ecommerce, an ad platform, and consent management tools for complete customer visibility.

## [56] Salesforce Commerce Cloud 101: Key Features and Benefits
Source: https://magicfuse.co/blog/what-is-salesforce-commerce-cloud

By 2025, eCommerce will become a $7+ trillion industry. By 2027, the number of online shoppers will reach 289 million, and eCommerce will account for nearly one-quarter of global retail sales. Considering the fast development of the eCommerce market and interest in online shopping, more and more retailers use the Salesforce Commerce Cloud platform to run their business processes for their online and physical stores together.

In turn, among the prevalent eCommerce trends for 2025 are:

Generative AI
Social commerce in conjunction with conversational commerce
Focus on sustainability
Headless commerce and PWAs
Personalized advertising

With Commerce Cloud, you can follow them all, increase sales, and drive customer satisfaction. This innovative Salesforce eCommerce solution enables you to scale your business, expand geographical boundaries, and present your brand globally.

This article will teach you how Salesforce Commerce Cloud can help eCommerce businesses grow and flourish. Buckle up, and let's explore what is Salesforce Commerce Cloud.

What is Salesforce Commerce Cloud?

Let's start with the backstory.

In 2016, Salesforce acquired Demandware, an eCommerce cloud-based provider for both large and small businesses. Combining Demandware with the Salesforce platform was a major step in transforming how eCommerce companies connect with their customers.

Salesforce created a new Salesforce Commerce Cloud using Demandware technology and added it to its Customer Success Platform.

Salesforce Commerce Cloud is a cloud-based ecommerce platform with various out-of-the-box features, useful tools, and commerce portals for growing your online business. It allows you to streamline the purchasing process, connect B2C and B2B, personalize your buying experience, and create a mobile-friendly shopping experience.

Considering that 32% of customers state that they will abandon a brand after one poor experience, the need to deliver a consistent, connected, and data-driven e-commerce experience is at an all-time high.

Let's take a closer look at the cloud-based commerce platform's main components and commerce functionality in Salesforce Digital 360:

Salesforce Commerce Cloud Main Features

Let's explore the main features of the platform and see how you can benefit from its use.

Unified Commerce Platform

In 2024, Salesforce introduced the next generation of Commerce Cloud - a platform that unifies every element of commerce, such as B2C, DTC, B2B Commerce, Order Management, Payments, and more. This unification is possible thanks to the APIs and modular microservices Salesforce relies on; they enable real-time synchronization between the front-end and back-end systems.

Research shows that adopting unified commerce data strategies presents a $1.5 trillion opportunity for business customers globally.

Michael Affronti, SVP and General Manager of Commerce Cloud, states that

"Commerce Cloud embodies unified commerce — giving businesses a single, integrated platform that brings every part of the commerce journey together with Agentforce agents to unlock new revenue opportunities and AI-powered efficiency, delivering consistent, personalized experiences across every channel."
Autonomous AI Agents: Agentforce

Salesforce also introduced three new Agents for Commerce - Merchant, Buyer, and Personal Shopper. These agents are designed to autonomously manage a range of tasks, including product recommendations and order lookup, without the need for direct human supervision.

Agentforce Agents use CRM data, external data, and metadata to autonomously manage tasks while maintaining the highest security and privacy guidelines.

Agents for Commerce include:

Agentforce Merchant. This agent works autonomously with ecommerce merchandisers to help them build and manage their commerce sites. It has an easy, conversational setup and goal setting. Merchants can handle tasks like generating personalized promotions or writing product descriptions, streamlining everyday actions within the workflow to improve efficiency and outcomes.
Agentforce Personal Shopper. This agent uses generative artificial intelligence to provide personalized assistance on ecommerce sites, chat, and messaging apps. It uses the retailer's catalog and product data to learn from shoppers' behavior and preferences.
Agentforce Buyer. This agent is designed to streamline the purchasing experience by providing proactive support and recommendations tailored to buyers' specific needs. It autonomously assists with tasks such as tracking orders, managing returns, and suggesting complementary products based on purchase history. Leveraging AI insights ensures buyers receive a seamless and highly personalized customer experience.
Salesforce Checkout

Salesforce Checkout offers a unified, one-click checkout experience connected to customer data on the Einstein 1 Platform. It includes built-in merchant services for payments, tax, and shipping, aiming to increase buyer conversion by providing a consistent experience across all customer touchpoints.

A partnership with Stripe and a new native integration with Adyen allows merchants to connect and use their existing payment provider through a  Bring Your Own Gateway (BYOG) model. Moreover, merchants can now offer more payment methods: PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Amazon Pay, and Link.

Headless Commerce Capabilities for B2B

Headless commerce is B2B architecture where the front-end (the customer interface) is separated from the back-end (product data, online sales, orders, and payments). As a result, businesses can make front-end updates independently.

Moreover, headless architectures are easily scalable, as updates to the front end can be made independently of the back end, allowing businesses to adapt quickly to changing market demands or increasing customer engagement needs.

Salesforce Commerce Cloud supports headless commerce through robust APIs, composable architecture, and AI-powered tools. These include:

Commerce APIs: Enable integration with external platforms and facilitate real-time communication between the front-end and back-end.
Agentforce Autonomous Agents: Assist with automating tasks like product recommendations and personalized assistance, providing tailored experiences to B2B buyers. Agentforce Personal Shopper uses product metadata to train AI models.
Einstein GPT: Delivers AI-driven insights and content personalization for a more engaging and intelligent shopping experience. Moreover, Einstein GPT’s predictive analytics help reduce cart abandonment rates.
Scalable Infrastructure: Salesforce’s cloud-based system ensures reliability and high performance, even for large-scale B2B operations.
Composable Commerce Enhancements for B2C

Salesforce continues to refine its composable commerce features, allowing businesses to build and deploy personalized B2C commerce experiences faster. With new APIs and advanced personalization options, developers can assemble tailored solutions that align with their unique customer requirements. This approach provides flexibility and scalability, making it easier to adapt to evolving consumer behaviors.

In-Store Inventory Planning

Leveraging Salesforce Data Cloud, the platform now offers real-time insights into inventory levels across multiple locations.

This feature provides accurate stock availability data for both online and in-store customers, using real-time customer data to help businesses optimize inventory management and meet consumer expectations. The real-time aspect ensures businesses can respond promptly to changes in demand, reducing lost sales due to out-of-stock items.

Enhanced Composable Storefront Architecture

Salesforce Commerce Cloud's Enhanced Composable Storefront Architecture provides a powerful, flexible solution for businesses looking to adopt headless commerce. A composable storefront acts as an all-in-one platform, enabling companies to create Progressive Web Apps (PWAs) that offer the speed and user engagement of native apps combined with the broad reach of the web.

This architecture supports auto-scaling, built-in security, and modern web technologies, ensuring 99.99% uptime, robust protection, and effortless scalability. With its modular design, businesses can implement changes in high-impact areas of their sites while maintaining existing storefront templates for other sections, reducing costs and risk.

Slack Integration

Salesforce Commerce Cloud integrates with Slack to streamline collaboration across commerce teams. This feature allows team members to share real-time updates on order statuses, inventory levels, and customer insights directly within Slack channels. Businesses can resolve issues faster, respond to customer needs more effectively, and ensure smooth operations during peak sales periods.

Einstein GPT Integration

Einstein GPT for Commerce combines Salesforce’s proprietary AI models with generative AI technology and real-time data from Salesforce Data Cloud to transform customer experiences.

The tool leverages unified customer data to automate and personalize key aspects of the shopping journey. For example, generating tailored product recommendations, creating unique product descriptions, and designing custom promotional offers.

Paired with the new drag-and-drop Page Designer for Composable Storefronts, businesses can create dynamic landing pages and headless commerce to create personalized shopping experiences without relying on third-party content management systems.

Integration into Salesforce Digital 360

In September 2020, Salesforce launched Digital 360, a comprehensive solution for marketing, commerce, and digital leaders. It allows business owners to adapt their businesses to today's all-digital reality by digitizing their brand-customer relationships and providing personalized customer experiences.

Digital 360 unifies key components of Marketing Cloud, Experience Cloud, and Commerce Cloud and brings innovations to the Salesforce Customer 360 platform.

As an integrated part of Digital 360, Commerce Cloud enables businesses to simplify the payment process and make checkout experience more secure. Thanks to the partnership with Stripe, you can use Commerce Cloud Payments to add payment functionality to your website with clicks, not code.

Your customers will be able to pay with credit cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay, mobile phones, and wallets, or they can choose non-card ways with integrated fraud protection.

Benefits of Using Commerce Cloud
Predictive Analytics

Salesforce Commerce Cloud leverages Einstein AI to empower businesses with predictive analytics that turn data into actionable insights. By analyzing customer behavior, purchase history, and preferences, businesses can forecast future trends, anticipate customer needs, and make informed decisions. For example, it can predict what a customer might purchase next or the type of product quality they expect.

Personalization

With Salesforce Commerce Cloud, personalization becomes a key driver of customer engagement and brand loyalty. The platform allows businesses to transform routine shopping interactions into meaningful experiences by tailoring content, recommendations and offers to individual preferences. Personalized experiences increase customer retention, improve satisfaction, and drive higher sales.

Multitenant Cloud Platform

Salesforce Commerce Cloud operates on a multitenant architecture, allowing businesses to share a unified software infrastructure while maintaining their unique environments. This setup ensures consistent access to the latest updates, seamless scalability, and reduced service disruptions. Businesses avoid the hassle of manual installations, with upgrades occurring three times a year automatically.

Easy Website Creation

This framework provides businesses with pre-designed wireframes, customizable templates, and commerce APIs to build commerce sites with ease. Developers and marketers alike can leverage these tools to craft dynamic and responsive sites that meet modern commerce demands. Businesses can launch professional-grade websites faster, saving time and reducing development costs while ensuring a seamless user experience.

Scalability

With Commerce Cloud, you can successfully cope with today's business challenges, such as high traffic, deep data storage, vast amounts of goods, and high transaction volumes. The platform allows you to implement new technologies and automatic scalability and seamlessly handle traffic spikes and other unforeseen events.

Unified Commerce

You can benefit from connecting the customer's entire shopping experience via digital channels, from marketing to successful purchase and retention campaigns.

Having information about each customer's interactions with your brand and shopping activities, you can personalize their journey and offer relevant product recommendations.

Mobile Optimisation

A mobile-optimized eCommerce store or a branded mobile app with a user-friendly interface is a must-have to attract customers and make their shopping experience pleasant and friction-free.

What's more, Google primarily checks the mobile version of the content to index and rank your website in organic search results. The tool is focused on cutting-edge technologies and takes a mobile-first approach.

What Types of Companies Are Recommended to Use Commerce Cloud?

Cloud Commerce meets B2C and B2B companies' needs. It offers two commerce products – B2C Commerce and B2B Commerce for consumer brands and retailers.

Both B2C business buyers and B2B businesses want to deliver an excellent eCommerce experience to their customers via eCommerce websites, so they need to utilize different practical tools.

B2C Commerce is used to manage eCommerce sites with a large number of guest shoppers and enhance the customer shopping experience. In turn, Salesforce B2B Commerce is aimed at satisfying the needs of B2B buyers who make large or frequent purchases and providing them with premium experiences.

Commerce Cloud is mostly used by companies with 50-200 employees and $1M-10M in revenue.

Engage Alerts. Using this real-time Salesforce service, you’ll get the data about prospects and customer activity from the past four days. ## [58] What is Salesforce Journey Builder and Why Marketers Use It
Source: https://magicfuse.co/blog/what-is-salesforce-journey-builder-and-why-marketers-use-it

Nowadays, the market is full of different products and services. To stand out from the crowd, you need to provide an excellent customer experience and take into account your prospect's needs and expectations. According to Salesforce’s State of the Connected customer report 2019, 66% of customers are willing to pay more for a great experience. It’s an excellent point for you. Map out a holistic, automated customer journey in Salesforce Journey Builder and be always in touch with your audience via different marketing channels.

From this article, you’ll learn about Salesforce Journey Builder and what its benefits you can use to increase customer satisfaction. You’ll discover the difference between Salesforce Journey and Automation Studio. Moreover, you’ll get a comprehensive guide on how to build an efficient journey, and thus to retain customers easily and quickly.

What Is Salesforce Journey Builder?

Salesforce Journey is one of Salesforce Marketing Cloud’s integrated tools for improving customer relationships. It’s a marketing automation solution for building consistent 1-to-1 customer journeys based on the data modelled in the Marketing Cloud.

Do you want your customers to download the app? Or, do you want them to make purchases successfully and not to leave abandoned carts? Then, Salesforce Journey Builder is here for your needs.

Track customer behaviour and boost your digital marketing across varied channels (email, SMS, Push and Ads). You can create a personalised fast-track communication plans by adding particular items (activities) from the Journey Builder’s panel in a drag-and-drop way.

Also, it’s possible to set the goals and control whether or not customers actually meet those goals, whether or not they stay in the journey and continue to the end, or they’re ejected on a particular step. Besides, you can pull in audience decision splits and specify wait times between journey’s steps.

Difference Between Journey Builder and Automation Studio

Both Journey Builder and Automation Studio are useful tools available for Marketing Cloud users to do multi-step marketing and data management activities. It’s important to understand the difference between them and the unique options of each of them. Let’s determine how you can use Journey Builder vs. Automation Studio, and how they can work together.

Automation Studio is a marketing tool focused on extract, transform or load ETL capabilities. On this platform, you can import, enrich and segment your data from any external source, and build simple or multi-step automations.

Also, you’re allowed to manage recurring processes, such as SQL queries, weekly reports and simple email campaigns. In addition, it’s possible to build advanced segmentation (using advanced SQL queries and data filters) and form the contact lists for the custom journeys.

You can send marketing messages via multi channels using both Journey Builder and Automation Studio. But, in turn, with Journey Builder, your opportunities are wider. The key differences between Journey Builder and Automation Studio are:

In Journey Builder, you can track user behaviour in real-time and on an individual basis. In turn, in Automation Studio you should wait until a batch is automatically finished processing at a specific time.
In Journey Builder, it’s possible to use event/ action triggers to choose the way to respond to a customer (email, SMS, etc.). In Automation Studio, you can create a fixed path for your customers regardless of their actions and engagement level.
You can set goals and view built-in goal reports in Journey Builder, while Automation Studio doesn’t offer such an option.

As customers prefer a personalised approach during their interaction with a company, it makes sense to combine capabilities of both Journey Builder and Automation Studio. For example, in Automation Studio, you can create complex audience segmentation using the data from multiple sources and use it in customised journeys in Journey Builder.

How to Build a Journey in Journey Builder

Journey Builder has a reputation as a user-friendly tool with easy configuration. First of all, you need to add a title and description of the journey. You can create a customer journey in two ways: using a pre-made Journey Template or building your own path from scratch with the help of Journey Builder’s activity items.

Journey Builder’s dashboard consists of two blocks: Entry Sources and Activities. Pick the entry source for a particular journey and enrich your customer journey with engaging activities according to your purposes. Check out the list of available activities below: (the tab)

https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1nN2-Qj9R1bh9PzwmQECRzQc8p-VK-d-vyo-xddJd8oA/edit?usp=sharing

Finally, using the Journey Builder toolbar, you can manage the journey you’ve created. It’s possible to set a goal, define exit criteria, save, test, activate journey and much more.

How to Enter Prospects Into a Journey

Your prospects can be entered into a journey via one of the 6 entry sources:

Data Extension - You’re allowed to select a sendable data extension and admit contacts into a journey.
API Event - You can set up an API that admits users into a Marketing Cloud journey.
CloudPages - Use Salesforce Marketing Cloud hosted forms to admit Marketing cloud contacts into a journey utilising the CloudPages Form Submit Event
Audience entry - Select one of the Audience Builder audiences available in your account to admit contacts into a journey.
Salesforce Data - Enter your Salesforce contacts into the journey by following the instructions.
Event (being phased out) - Select this source in case you want to put contacts into a journey based on their behaviour (e.g. a customer purchases a product, a contact signs up for a newsletter, a user provides his review).
Pro Tips For Using Journey Builder

Start with a simple journey. If you’re a newbie user of Journey Builder, it’s recommended to create at first like a thank you follow-up email or a happy birthday message. Also, it’s better to use simple options at first, e.g. the Welcome Sequence or Timed Waits before extending to Decision Splits.

On the other hand, you can turn to full-cycle Salesforce development and consulting company to get professional help with it. MagicFuse is one of such Salesforce customization companies. They provide high-quality services focused on the technical side of Salesforce.

Plan your journey on paper and prepare all necessary data and content. Before creating a real journey it matters to map your journey visually. In such a way, you can structure your journey and include all the needed steps. Moreover, collect the information that will be used in the journey.

Test your journey. When a final version of your journey is ready, it’s recommended to clone it before activating. Then, test your plan and improve if necessary. Also, it’s important to check time settings and avoid conflicts between data updates and automation.

Save your time and use copied activities. Create a “Copied Activities Clipboard” in the Journey Builder panel and drag the bundle of icons on the canvas to create your customer journeys. This option allows you to decrease your time to design a plan from scratch.

No autosave option. Journey Builder doesn’t provide autosave. So, remember about it and save your journey in the process.

Use the Goals feature to measure journey performance. It’s a great opportunity to gather performance metrics and analyse how to interact and convert potential customers.

Remove prospects easily. Using the Exit Criteria option, you can exclude a prospect from the journey, e.g. if their status changes or they become a cold lead.

Summary

Creating a positive customer experience is the number one priority. Managing customer experience has to be your main task. With Salesforce Journey Builder, you’ll be able to build both simple and complex customer journeys, thus improving customer retention and satisfaction, cross-selling and up-selling.

FAQ

Journey in Salesforce Marketing Cloud refers to Journey Builder, that is a visual tool for creating, managing, and automating customer journeys across different channels, such as email, mobile, social, and web.

The benefits of using Journey Builder include:

Increased conversions and revenue: By delivering the right message to the right person at the right time, brands can increase the likelihood of customers taking action and making a purchase.

Time and cost savings: By automating the customer journey, marketers can save time and resources and focus on other important tasks, such as creating compelling content or analyzing campaign performance.

Better insights and analytics: Journey Builder provides detailed analytics and reporting on customer interactions and campaign performance, enabling marketers.

What is the use of Journey Builder in Salesforce?

Journey Builder in Salesforce is used to create and manage customer journeys across different channels and touchpoints. It defines the steps and actions that a customer will take in response to specific triggers, such as opening an email, clicking on a link, or visiting a website to personalize the content and messaging based on customer data and preferences, and test and optimize the campaigns for better results.

What Is Pardot?

Pardot is the 7th most popular in the Top 1 Million sites in the Marketing Automation category. It’s a smart B2B marketing automation solution included in the Salesforce Marketing Cloud’s toolset. Marketers use it to provide the sales department and generate high-quality leads.

In turn, sales reps can close more deals faster based on the provided information. Thus, your marketers have an opportunity to collaborate with the sales team quickly and efficiently using Pardot’s functionality.

With Pardot you can move your customers through a sales funnel:

Lead generation (creating interest and demand for your product);
Conversion (visitors interact with your website and provide you with their contact data);
Lead nurturing (reaching prospects through sending targeted messages across different channels based on the user’s actions);
Lead qualification (marketers select the cream of the prospects (based on score and grade metrics) and sales reps follow up with them).

Using the Pardot system, you can design stunning emails, engage your target audience with relevant content, track user’s each step and capture marketing ROI, enhance customer experience and generate data-driven solutions for your business growth.

How Pardot Can Help With Marketing Automation

Lead generation

Besides, you can get a complete picture of your social media marketing campaigns and interactions with your audience via social platforms thanks to Pardot's functionality.

Lead management

Pardot lets you be in touch with your audience via messaging based on particular triggers, such as interactions, time and other custom parameters. With this marketing tool, you can collect the hottest leads based on scoring and grading metrics about users. Pardot automatically divides the prospects into targeted, dynamic lists. Pardot helps you track your customers’ behaviour and interests, so you’ll be able to offer relevant, dynamic content.

Email marketing

Pardot allows performing email marketing campaigns efficiently and effectively. With a user-friendly, visual Email Builder, you can build bright, responsive emails tailored according to your customers’ requirements.

Pardot has useful features, such as visual nurturing canvas, schedule option and autoresponders to automate a customer engagement process. With this tool, you can personalise and send relevant messages to your customers, collect the statistics about deliverability and best-performing content.

Alignment with Development

One of the main advantages of using Pardot is an opportunity to connect marketing and sales reps to reach excellent results in customer engagement campaigns. ROI Reporting

With Pardot, you can analyse the impact of your marketing and sales efforts on revenue. Pardot creates different types of reporting, such as ROI Reporting, Lifecycle Reporting, Advanced Email Reporting. Moreover, it’s possible to connect various marketing tools that you use and manage interaction with customers across channels.

Artificial Intelligence

Using artificial intelligence integrated into Pardot, you can improve your marketing and sales efforts and engage more leads. With the Pardot Einstein tool, it’s available to monitor and analyse lead scoring, customer behaviour scoring, user engagement activity, and marketing campaign insights. Machine learning allows you to find qualified leads, view influence fields, use a customer-centric approach and discover new audiences.

How Pardot and Salesforce Work Together

As Pardot is a Salesforce marketing automation solution, it has native integration with Salesforce CRM. You can get the Pardot app from the AppExchange marketplace, install and configure it in your Salesforce CRM, and verify the connector in Pardot for enabling integration. The Salesforce connector allows synchronising and interchanging the data between Pardot and Salesforce. Pardot asks for updates from Salesforce every 2-4 minutes, so information is presented in real-time.

The contact records are synchronised by an email address, as an identifier. If the match isn’t found in the Salesforce database, a new record will be created. In case of information conflict, a record in Salesforce overrides the Pardot one.

Depending on the fields you’ve customised between Pardot and Salesforce while setting up the connector, specific data will be synced. Aside from that, it’s possible to assign prospects to Salesforce marketing campaigns, set tasks for the sales department, and view reports about campaigns directly in Pardot.

You can find out more detailed information about how to connect Pardot and Salesforce in the Salesforce tutorial.

## [61] What is Salesforce Product Development Outsourcer (PDO)?
Source: https://magicfuse.co/blog/what-is-salesforce-product-development-outsourcer-pdo

Introduction

Salesforce market is growing very fast these years. It is estimated that in 2020 the Salesforce ecosystem will be worth around 73 billion U.S. dollars. More and more enterprises and companies adopt Salesforce every day. That creates an entire world around Salesforce products, services, consultants, and startups. As many of you know, many Salesforce customization companies and AppExchange ISV products are official partners of Salesforce. On a global scale, there are more than 1300 consulting companies and more than 3600 ISV apps.

Of course, various consultants and ISVs have different industry or service competencies. However, almost all of them face some cases when there is a need for custom Salesforce app development, package creation & deployment, security review, or Salesforce integration with other APIs, products, or internal systems.

In these cases, Salesforce consultants and ISVs either handle this work with their own in-house Salesforce developers or go to a particular group of Salesforce Consultants called PDOs — Product Development Outsourcing companies. PDO is a very new and unique type of Salesforce partner that is 100% focused on the technical side of Salesforce. So, in this article, we will shed more light on what PDO is, what types of PDO exist, and how to find a PDO company on AppExchange.

Based on our research, there are less than 20 Salesforce PDO companies worldwide in Q4 2019.
What is Salesforce PDO company?

According to Salesforce, Product Development Outsourcers (PDOs) represent a broad spectrum of consulting partners and vendors with expertise in building commercial apps and other valuable services like training, funding, marketing, or selling your app. These specialized partners can help architect & design a commercial app, tackle specific areas of your build (like third-party integrations).

In other words, Salesforce PDOs aim to handle all the technical issues, integrations with 3rd party services, technical implementation or configuration, or custom component development. Even though these companies primarily focus on the technical side of Salesforce, they can also serve as a team extension for other Salesforce partners that miss sufficient Salesforce development capabilities.

What are the main benefits of Salesforce PDOs?
Salesforce PDOs can handle the whole technical scope of any Salesforce project from the discovery phase to AppExchange app development, deployment, or delivery for implementation projects.
As PDOs work mainly with custom development, integrations, and app deployments, you can focus on principal business and product challenges. The advantage of having a PDO on your team is that they will consider security throughout the development process, not just at the beginning or conclusion.
Usually, PDOs work in conjunction with your business team so that you can avoid any issues in the area of technical project requirements.
PDOs can handle the Salesforce security review process if there is an ISV case.
PDOs can work on multiple projects simultaneously if they work with other Salesforce consulting companies that miss development capacity or expertise.
If you work with offshore or nearshore Salesforce PDOs, you can decrease the costs and increase the project's profitability.
PDOs provide you with insider information on product strategies, allowing you to make sensible business decisions that will help your application stand out from the crowd.
PDOs can also help to transfer all technical documentation, so your clients can use it for further needs with other partners, codebase updates and improvements, or different integrations.
PDOs can help you to conduct a successful technical pre-sales process and correctly evaluate the project timelines and budget.
What types of Salesforce PDOs exist?

Even if Salesforce PDO is a subcategory of the Salesforce Consulting Partner group, there are certain levels and clusters for these PDO companies. In general, there are four main tiers for Salesforce PDO organizations.

Certified Specialist
Certified Navigator
Specialist Navigator
Masters Navigator

The main difference between them is the partnership status represented in search filtering on AppExchange plus some additional domain expertise inside of Salesforce ecosystem. The requirements are different for each level. Also, PDO program has specialization directories for these partners that become available for the top 2 PDO tiers — Specialist Navigator and Masters Navigator. You can see the full list of possible specializations below. Some specialties are not within the PDO Master selection on the project/story submission form. That is because it is a specialization within another Product Master. The ones that start with PDO are specific to the PDO Masters.

PDO: Integration / Connects Apps / Lightning Connect
PDO: Security Review & AppExchange Listing
PDO: Namespaces / Managed Packages
PDO: LMA / COA / Environment Hub
Custom App Dev — Process
PDO: Trialforce
PDO: Lightning Components
PDO: Einstein Analytics
PDO: Shield
Salesforce Platform: Custom App Dev — Coding
Salesforce Platform: Large Data Volumes (over 5 Million Records in the org)
Salesforce Platform: Heroku Application Development and Data Services
Salesforce Platform: Mobile Customer App Dev (Salesforce SDK/Force)
Community Cloud: Self-Service Community (B2C/B2B)
How to find Salesforce PDOs on AppExchange?

The AppExchange platform has a filter for AppExchange App Development. Also, your Salesforce Partner Account Managers and other Technical Evangelists can refer to proper PDOs that best fit specific requirements.

The AppExchange platform includes a filter that is utilized in the building of AppExchange apps. Salesforce account managers or technical evangelists might recommend the best PDOs for specific purposes.

Who is responsible for PDOs at Salesforce?

Based on the publicly available information, we found three people at Salesforce who are involved in the partner process related to PDO program.

Verity Denman — EMEA Senior Partner Program Manager at Salesforce
Ravi Ravichandran — Architect at Salesforce
Marc Kuster — Director, AppExchange & ISV Technical Enablement EMEA at Salesforce.
To sum up

PDOs are a feasible route to market for AppExchange Applications. They enable organizations that use AppExchange to facilitate integrations by getting your software onto the marketplace fast and at a low cost.

You will witness quicker time-to-market, meaningful user engagement, and accelerated growth for your Salesforce AppExchange product through our trusted delivery methodology, Salesforce architecture knowledge, and entire product life cycle strategy.

To recap, PDO can:

drive customer adoption by providing a consistent Salesforce customer experience that expands as your company grows
create a profitable business with a bespoke product built on Salesforce and designed with results-oriented KPIs
expand your product into Salesforce AppExchange and enter a new market with a partner that can assist you in determining the best product-market fit

FAQ
What is PDO in Salesforce?

A PDO is a Salesforce employee who is assigned to work with Salesforce partners to help them build and grow their Salesforce practice. The role of a PDO is to provide partners with strategic guidance, technical support, and business development resources to help them succeed.

What are benefits of Salesforce PDOs?

Working with a Salesforce PDO can provide numerous benefits for partners, including: Access to specialized Salesforce expertise and resources. Guidance on best practices for building and growing a Salesforce practice. Assistance with technical issues and implementation challenges. Help with developing sales and marketing strategies to reach new clients. Increased credibility with clients due to the partnership with Salesforce.

What are types of Salesforce PDOs?

Each type of PDO has a specific focus and provides different types of support to partners. Regional PDOs work with partners in specific geographic regions to provide localized support and resources, while industry-specific PDOs have specialized knowledge and experience in specific industries. Technical PDOs provide technical guidance and support, while business development PDOs help partners with sales and marketing strategies, lead generation, and other business development activities.
